text: Woe to you, destroyer, who have not been destroyed; you traitor, whom no one has betrayed! When you finish destroying, you will be destroyed; when you stop betraying, you will be betrayed.
LORD, be gracious to us; we long for you. Be their arm every morning, our salvation in time of distress.

versions.text: LORD, be gracious to us; we have waited for you. Be our strength every morning, our salvation in time of distress.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads "their arm" (זְרֹעָם), shifting from second to third person; "our strength" silently harmonizes the pronoun. Either restore the Hebrew reading or retain the smoother reading with a footnote such as "Hebrew: their arm."

text: At the sound of the tumult the peoples flee; when you rise up, the nations scatter.

versions.text: At the thunder of your voice the peoples flee; when you rise up, the nations scatter.
versions.explanation: הָמוֹן means "tumult, uproar, roar of a multitude"; "your voice" is not in the Hebrew of the first clause (the second-person suffix appears only in the second clause).

text: Your plunder is gathered as young locusts gather; like a swarm of locusts they rush upon it.

versions.text: Your plunder is gathered as the caterpillar gathers; men swarm over it like a swarm of locusts.
versions.explanation: "Caterpillar" for חָסִיל is archaic and clashes with the locust imagery in the second line; "men" is added and unnecessary. The revision keeps a single, consistent image and reads more smoothly aloud.

text: The LORD is exalted, for he dwells on high; he has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
He will be the sure foundation of your times, a wealth of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge; the fear of the LORD is Zion's treasure.
Look, their heroes cry aloud in the streets; the envoys of peace weep bitterly.
The highways lie deserted; no traveler is on the road. The treaty is broken, its witnesses despised, and no one is held in regard.

versions.text: The highways lie deserted; no traveler is on the road. The treaty is broken, its witnesses despised, and no one is regarded.
versions.explanation: "Witnesses" follows a variant reading; the traditional Hebrew text has "cities" (עָרִים). A footnote such as "Or: cities; the traditional Hebrew text reads cities" would be helpful. "No one is held in regard" also flows better than the clipped "no one is regarded."

versions.text: The treaty is broken, its witnesses despised, and no one is held in regard.
versions.explanation: The first half of the Hebrew verse (נָשַׁמּוּ מְסִלּוֹת שָׁבַת עֹבֵר אֹרַח, "the highways lie desolate, the wayfarer has ceased") was dropped in the last revision. It must be restored; the second clause about the broken treaty and the improved "held in regard" are retained as intentionally revised.

text: The land mourns and languishes; Lebanon is ashamed and withers away. Sharon has become like the desert, and Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.
"Now I will arise," says the LORD. "Now I will lift myself up; now I will be exalted.
You conceive chaff, you give birth to straw; your breath is a fire that will devour you.
The peoples will be burned to lime, like thornbushes cut down and set ablaze.
Hear, you who are far off, what I have done; and you who are near, acknowledge my might.
The sinners in Zion are terrified; trembling grips the godless: "Who among us can dwell with a devouring fire? Who among us can dwell with everlasting flames?"

The one who walks righteously and speaks what is right, who rejects gain from extortion and keeps his hands from taking bribes, who stops his ears against plots of murder and shuts his eyes against looking on evil—
he will dwell on the heights; his refuge will be a fortress of rock. His bread will be given him, and his water will not fail.
Your eyes will see the king in his beauty and behold a land that stretches far away.
Your heart will ponder the former terror: "Where is the scribe? Where is the one who weighed the tribute? Where is the officer who counted the towers?"
You will no longer see that insolent people, that people of obscure speech beyond understanding, stammering in a tongue you cannot grasp.
Look on Zion, the city of our appointed feasts; your eyes will see Jerusalem, a peaceful home, a tent that will not be moved. Its stakes will never be pulled up, nor any of its ropes broken.
But there the LORD in his majesty will be for us a place of broad rivers and streams, where no galley with oars will travel and no mighty ship will pass.

versions.text: There the LORD will be our Mighty One—a place of broad rivers and streams, where no galley with oars will travel, no mighty ship will pass.
versions.explanation: In the Hebrew, אַדִּיר describes the LORD ("the majestic LORD"), and what he is "for us" is the place of broad rivers; the current dash makes the rivers an awkward appositive to "our Mighty One."

text: For the LORD is our judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our king; he will save us.
Your rigging hangs slack: the mast is not held firm, the sail is not spread. Then an abundance of spoil will be divided, and even the lame will carry off plunder.
And no one living there will say, "I am sick"; the people who dwell in her will be forgiven their sin.
